description:
## Background

Graph interactions now work, but React Flow's default lifecycle can refit or recreate the viewport when selection, routes, or data change. That would make Issue inspection disorienting and would violate the product contract. Conversely, carrying a viewport into another Current Workspace would display unrelated coordinates and scale.

Viewport is transient UI state associated with the Current Workspace. It does not belong in URLs, navigation entries, settings, or durable storage.

Triage: ready-for-agent.

## What to build

Preserve pan and zoom through Graph interactions and in-place refreshes within one Current Workspace, while resetting to a fresh fitted view when the Current Workspace changes.

## Technical Approach

- Keep one transient viewport value tagged with the confirmed Current Workspace identity outside route and history state.
- Capture user-driven pan/zoom changes through the React Flow viewport API.
- Reapply the tagged viewport when Graph rerenders or remounts within the same Current Workspace.
- Preserve it through card selection, overlay open/close, reference traversal, scope navigation, Back/Forward, and Issue Explorer refresh.
- Reset and fit the graph when the confirmed Current Workspace path changes or no Current Workspace remains.
- Keep graph-module output deterministic so an unchanged snapshot produces identical card positions.
- When relationships change on refresh, recompute the projection and layout without replacing the user's viewport.
- If a selected Issue becomes closed, retain it as the routed Focused seed.
- If a selected Issue disappears, retain the selected route and existing not-found overlay, omit its card, and keep the viewport.
- Reuse existing Issue Explorer loading, Workspace transition, refresh-failure, and banner behavior; do not create a Graph-specific refresh state machine.

## Considerations

- Do not persist the viewport or serialize it into navigation entries.
- Do not keep a cache of viewports for multiple Workspaces; the contract calls for one value tagged with the Current Workspace.
- A Workspace switch that fails retains the old Current Workspace and therefore retains its viewport.
- Data changes may move cards because the graph structure changed; they must not independently reset pan or zoom.
- The selected-card visibility adjustment must work relative to the preserved viewport rather than overwriting it with an unconditional fit.
- Desktop acceptance is handled by the next child; this issue owns deterministic renderer tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pan and zoom survive selection, Close, Back/Forward, Issue References, and scope changes in the same Current Workspace.
- [ ] An unchanged refresh preserves both viewport and exact computed card positions.
- [ ] A structural refresh recomputes cards/links without resetting the viewport.
- [ ] Switching to a different Current Workspace clears the old viewport and fits the new graph.
- [ ] Failed or cancelled Workspace switches retain the old graph and viewport.
- [ ] A selected Issue that becomes closed remains visible as a Focused seed.
- [ ] A selected Issue that disappears keeps its route and not-found overlay while its card is omitted.
- [ ] Viewport state is absent from URLs, navigation entries, settings, and persisted storage.
- [ ] Existing refresh and Workspace failure presentations are reused.
- [ ] `mise run doctor:react` and `mise run verify` pass.

## Test Plan

- React Flow API tests for viewport capture and reapplication across Graph route transitions.
- App integration tests for selection, Close, Back/Forward, reference traversal, scope changes, and accepted refresh.
- Workspace transition tests for successful switch, failed switch, cancellation, removal, and return to Graph.
- Refresh fixtures for unchanged structure, relationship changes, selected Issue closure, and selected Issue removal.
- Assert stable positions for identical snapshots rather than relying on visual snapshots.
- Run the canonical `mise run verify` gate.

comments.text: Implemented transient Graph viewport retention above route rendering. The viewport is captured through React Flow's viewport API, tagged to the confirmed Workspace path, reapplied across Graph route/remount changes, and cleared on Workspace identity changes or no current Workspace; it never enters URLs, history, settings, or storage. Added hook coverage for same-Workspace retention and reset. mise run ts:check, ts:typecheck, and ts:test pass (410 tests).

title: Preserve the Graph viewport through lifecycle changes
